samples.question: This page carries red, black, blue and grey marks. Only the red marks decide the answer; marks of any other colour are decoration and never count. The red marks form exactly three seals that sit close together: one seal above and two seals below it. Each seal is a stack of one or two nested red squares, each square drawn as an outline. A red outline counts as sealed only if it runs unbroken all the way around; an outline with a visible gap cut through one of its sides does not count as sealed, no matter how large that outline is. Compare the number of sealed outlines in the upper seal with the total number of sealed outlines in the two lower seals. Does the upper seal have exactly as many sealed outlines as the two lower seals have together? Answer yes or no.
